questions.question: A single 2/0 R90 aluminum-sheathed copper conductor is run in free air. What is its ampacity?
references: Table 3 (single conductor in free air, 90°C column)
solution_steps: It is ONE conductor in FREE AIR → Rule 4-004 1)a) sends you to the free-air ampacity table (Table 3 in the class notes).
Value = 300 A. No bundling or ambient correction is stated, so that is the answer.

questions.question: A rigid steel conduit contains three #4 R90 copper conductors and three #1 TW75 copper conductors. What is the maximum allowable ampacity of each conductor?
What is the maximum allowable ampacity of each conductor if there are 25 #4 R90 copper conductors installed in EMT?
An 800 A non-continuous load is supplied by paralleling single-conductor Teck cable, type RW90 copper, direct buried and spaced 190 mm apart. What is the minimum size required?
Determine the minimum size of copper NS75 neutral-supported cable required for a 200 A, 120/240 V, single-phase overhead service.
What is the maximum allowable ampacity of each conductor when there are two 2/0 R90 XLPE aluminum conductors installed in a free-air run?
Does an electrician need to count bonding conductors when determining the ampacities of conductors in raceways?
questions.answer: No — bonding conductors are not counted as current-carrying conductors.

questions.question: What is the maximum ampacity of each conductor when 10 #4 R90 Cu conductors are installed in a run of EMT located in a 40°C ambient temperature?
solution_steps: Base ampacity: #4 copper at 90°C (R90), Table 2 = 95 A.
95 × 0.70 × 0.91 ≈ 60.5 A. (Always derate from the 90°C base, then check terminations.)

questions.question: What are the required colours of conductors installed in a 3-phase, 3-wire, 600 V circuit?
If a #6 Teck90 cable is terminated at a circuit breaker marked maximum 75°C, what is the maximum current this cable can carry?
solution_steps: Rule 4-006: even with a 90°C cable, the ampacity is limited by the lowest-rated termination — here 75°C.
Read #6 copper in the 75°C column of Table 2 = 65 A.
